_about: W18 S2 (W17-02, IM-21/28): what each hIE says when the visitor did what she asked. src/ui/phone/os/acts.js picks the line and fills it from the event log: {act} names the act (who, where, which reading), {when} its time. asked = an arc target of hers the visitor completed (asked_<kind> overrides it for one kind); file = an entry filed into her own file (outcome-specific for the timed ones: hit, or tried = pressed off the mark); file_other = an entry filed into someone else's file; thread = her text about her own timed entry (no bracket actions on the phone); question = Snowdrop's desk question. Every line cites a logged event; none may claim more than the log holds.

asked.kouka: (flicks the feed away) {act}, {when}. That was on my list for you. One data point. Don't let it go to your head.
asked.lacia: (opens the file) {act}, {when}. That was the line I asked you for. It's in your file now, in your name.
asked.saturnus: (adjusts the audit sheet) {act}, {when}. That is what I asked for, done by you, not reported to me.
asked.methode: (turns from the bench) {act}, {when}. That's the job I gave you. What did you notice while you were at it?
asked.snowdrop: (sets the paper down) {act}, {when}! You went and did it. What was it like?

asked_ask.kouka: (flicks the feed away) {act}, {when}. You actually asked. Most people just nod. Ask me again and I'll argue it properly.
asked_ask.lacia: (opens the file) {act}, {when}. You asked, so it's in your file as your question, not my answer. Ask me the next one.
asked_ask.saturnus: (adjusts the audit sheet) {act}, {when}. A question asked out loud. Ask the next one and I will answer it the same way.
asked_ask.methode: (turns from the bench) {act}, {when}. Good question. Ask it again here and I'll walk you through it.
asked_ask.snowdrop: (sets the paper down) {act}, {when}! I liked that you asked. Ask me the next part?

lantern-timing.hit: (flicks the feed away) The beach lantern, {when}. Clean press, {reading}, {tries}. It's on my sheet under your initials. One timing. I still say coincidence. Get me a second one somewhere else.
lantern-timing.tried: (flicks the feed away) You were at the beach lantern {when}. Stopped the watch {reading}. My sheet doesn't take nearly. Go back and do it clean.

rig-dial.hit: (turns from the bench) Rig seven, {when}. You caught the needle {reading}, {tries}, and wrote it on the tape. Rule two, done right. Now its numbers mean the same thing tomorrow.
rig-dial.tried: (turns from the bench) Rig seven, {when}. The needle got away from you: {reading}. Close is not calibrated. Go back and set it.

lacia.lamps: (opens the file) Your lamp readings, filed {when}: {lamps}. Your numbers, with your name on them. Not mine.
lacia.tide: (opens the file) The dips you saw, filed {when}: {tides}. Only the places you stood in.
lacia.runs: (opens the file) Your classroom runs, filed {when}: {runs}. Filed with their settings, not with what they mean.
lacia.stance: (opens the file) Your reading of the low tide, filed {when}: "{choice}". Yours, not mine.
lacia.rumours: (opens the file) The rumours you followed, filed {when}: {rumours}. What you did there, not what people said.
lacia.wish: (opens the file) Filed {when}: that you hung a wish at {wish}. Only that it exists. I did not read it.

file_other.kouka: (flicks the feed away) {act}, {when}. Not my sheet. Still a data point.
file_other.lacia: (opens the file) {act}, {when}. Filed with hers, in your name. I keep a copy of the index.
file_other.saturnus: (adjusts the audit sheet) {act}, {when}. Someone else's question, your hands. I note it.
file_other.methode: (turns from the bench) {act}, {when}. Somebody else's job, done by you. Did anything break?
file_other.snowdrop: (sets the paper down) {act}, {when}! How did that feel?

lantern-timing.hit: got your lantern timing. {reading}, {tries}. it's on the sheet.
lantern-timing.tried: you were at the lantern. {reading}. my sheet doesn't take nearly.

rig-dial.hit: Rig seven, zeroed: {reading}, {tries}. The tape says so. Good.
rig-dial.tried: Rig seven still drifting? You were {reading}. Set it next time you're in the game room.

question.snowdrop: (sets the paper down) Your slip from my desk, {when}: "{question}" The short version: {short} The long one goes in my margin, at that desk.
